newsitem.title: LEBANON: Lebanon's BLOM bank buys French, Swiss banks.
newsitem.headline: Lebanon's BLOM bank buys French, Swiss banks.

text.p: Lebanon's Banque du Liban et d'Outre Mer (BLOM) said on Wednesday it had acquired all shares in Banque Banorabe-France which also fully owns Banque Banorient-Suisse.
The acquisition made BLOM "the Lebanese bank with the largest presence in major European and Arab financial centres," the bank said in a statement.
It said the acquisitions were in place by the end of 1996.
BLOM simultaneously announced that it had doubled its shareholders' equity at the end of 1996 to $150 million from $77 million, making it Lebanon's second biggest bank in terms of capital.

Banque de la Mediterranee, which is wholly owned by Prime Minister Rafik al-Hariri, holds the number one position after more than doubling its capital at the end of 1996 to $212 million from $102 million.
BLOM said its group now comprised the following legally independent units:
- Banque du Liban et d'Outre Mer SAL with 32 branches in Lebanon and an offshore unit in Cyprus,
- Banque d'Affaires du Liban et d'Outre Mer SAL, a specialised bank for medium- and long-term financing,
- Banque Banorabe SA, a French company based in Paris with capital and reserves totalling 266 million French francs, with branches in London, Dubai, Sharjah and Muscat,
- Banque Banorient SA, a Swiss company based in Geneva with capital and reserves exceeding 35 million Swiss francs.
